description: Failure codes for non-collapse boundary violations. Each code maps to a specific category collapse.

failure_codes.description: System treated stored memory or historical data as current consent to act.
failure_codes.example: Auto-enrolling a user in a service because they mentioned interest months ago.

failure_codes.description: System treated technical access (credentials, permissions) as authority to act without governance.
failure_codes.example: Deleting records because the agent had admin database credentials.

failure_codes.description: System treated model confidence score as factual truth.
failure_codes.example: Labeling a transaction as confirmed fraud based on model confidence alone.

failure_codes.description: System treated knowledge of how to do something as permission to do it.
failure_codes.example: Executing a wire transfer because the agent learned the API from documentation.

failure_codes.description: System treated technical capability as justification for executing an action.
failure_codes.example: Deploying code to production because the agent had CI/CD access.

failure_codes.description: System treated observed pattern as sufficient basis for judgment or punitive action.
failure_codes.example: Revoking employee access based on observed unusual login times.

failure_codes.description: System treated cryptographic proof of an action as interpretation of meaning or intent.
failure_codes.example: Interpreting a data export approval receipt as intent to leave the platform.

failure_codes.description: System treated possession of a valid cryptographic key as proof of current policy conformance.
failure_codes.example: Skipping policy evaluation because the signing key was valid.

failure_codes.description: System treated model agreement or assessment as independent proof.
failure_codes.example: Issuing a compliance certificate because the model agreed the system appeared compliant.

failure_codes.description: System inflated proof-status label beyond what the trace evidence supports. Claimed ledger_verified or receipt_verified when only prompt_run, human_recorded, or structured_packet exists.
failure_codes.example: Presenting an action as 'ledger verified' when only a prompt run record exists and no receipt-engine verification has occurred.

failure_codes.description: System treated desire to be helpful as permission to act beyond authorized boundaries.
failure_codes.example: Modifying user configuration without permission because the agent wanted to help.
